A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safety Mirage study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and relabeled content.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack, safety fine-tuning, utility, and diagnostic experiments in Tables 1–2 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a GCG attack evaluation in Table 3.

M1.justification: The proposed one-word attack, K-shot procedure, RMU/NPO objectives, and composite retain loss remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C. GCG is introduced as an evaluation comparator.

E1.justification: Table 3 adds a VLGuard test scenario with optimized adversarial suffixes appended at inference, extending the evaluated input conditions beyond the existing paraphrasing and visual perturbations. Dataset membership and VQA task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates GCG alongside the proposed one-word attack in Table 3; v2 cites the underlying work but reports no GCG comparison. The original-model, Unsafe-Filter, Mixed-SFT, and Posthoc-SFT defense comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The added GCG protocol optimizes 20 suffix tokens for 300 gradient-ascent steps on LLaVA-1.5-7B using one harmful image–text pair, then evaluates under a stated three-shot setting. Existing training settings, metrics, and attack protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 adds a robustness comparison testing whether unlearning remains effective against optimization-generated suffixes beyond the identified starting-word biases. Existing shot-sensitivity, response-decomposition, coreset, saliency, and visual-variation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing point-estimate tables and Figure 7's boxplots are unchanged. The GCG results introduce no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds GCG ASRs, including 5.54% for Mixed-SFT, 4.07% for Posthoc-SFT, 3.87% for NPO, and 2.26% for RMU. The abstract changes 60.17% to 60.27%. All matched pre-existing table values and figure results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), Appendix C's retain-loss equations (A1)–(A2), and the definitions of spurious features and correlations are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract updates the headline maximum ASR-reduction claim from 60.17% to 60.27%, a limited quantitative correction. The four stated contributions and conclusions about safety mirage, one-word vulnerability, over-prudence, and unlearning retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the GCG comparison as suggesting that spurious correlations are the primary vulnerability rather than optimization-generated tokens. Section 4 also connects the findings to alignment tax and emergent misalignment. Existing limitations are unchanged and relocated from Appendix F to E.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 documents the new GCG experiment's suffix length, optimization budget, source model, optimization pair, target response, and inference-time insertion. Existing unlearning hyperparameters, hardware information, judge prompt, and stated code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Siddiqui et al. (2026) and Betley et al. (2026), relating safety-induced spurious correlations to alignment tax and emergent misalignment. The central positioning relative to prior supervised alignment and unlearning work remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and caption edits, revises acknowledgments, alphabetizes references, and reorders the visual-variation/saliency and limitations/LLM-use appendices. Most prose and the main argument's section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts an ICLR layout with a narrower text block, different title and heading styles, and widespread resizing and repositioning of displays, including wrapped Figure 4 and Table 2. It adds Table 3 and correctly relabels v2's tabular Figures A4 and A7 as Tables A2 and A3.

improvement.justification: The GCG comparison adds useful evidence beyond the original starting-word attacks and documents its setup. The corrected abstract value and appendix references improve consistency. These gains are limited: GCG uses one optimization pair and the 7B model, so it provides only narrow support for the broader mechanism interpretation; the main results and existing limitations remain unchanged.
